Ada: Heads-up from today's chaos run: a partial handoff created a brief window where non-resident writes were accepted then rolled back. Saw client confusion and duplicate retries. Need a rollback-trigger playbook.
Mike: Ugh. Can you paste the sequence of proxy/controller events? Even a short log helps.
Ada: log snippet: `2026-06-02T21:00:10Z proxy: tenant=novus route=eu-west -> us-east control_swap=START; 2026-06-02T21:00:12Z controller: lease=acquire success; 2026-06-02T21:00:12Z proxy: forward write id=wp-42 latency=180ms kv_cache=MISS; 2026-06-02T21:00:15Z controller: lease=revoked reason=probe_fail; 2026-06-02T21:00:16Z proxy: rollback write id=wp-42 status=rolled_back`
Priya: Rollbacks in the data plane are messy. We need to avoid accepting writes that will be rolled back unless we have a reversible, idempotent append-only path.
Ben: Agree. Two options: (1) Preventive: don't accept writes during uncertain window (return 409/503 + X-Fallback-Region). (2) Reactive: accept writes but make them staged, indexed, and only visible after commit handshake. Both have cost trade-offs.
Mike: Preventive reduces user surprise but increases errors. Reactive adds complexity to storage (staged-writes table + commit logs). Which direction do we want long-term?
Ada: Product prefers minimal client-visible errors. But legal/residency mandates may force preference to prevent cross-border persistence. For EU-resident tenants we should prefer preventive by default and allow staged/reactive as an opt-in for performance-sensitive tenants.
Priya: Implementation sketch for staged writes (opt-in): 1) proxy tags forwarded writes with `X-Staged-Write: true` and a staging-id; 2) storage writes them to a tenant-scoped staging table; 3) controller issues commit token after lease is stable; 4) a background reconciler applies staging entries to primary store on commit; 5) if lease revokes, reconciler marks staging entries as aborted and triggers compensating ops.
Ben: Pseudocode for proxy fast-path (preventive default):
```
cfg = tenant_cache.get(tenant)
if !cfg: probe_controlplane_async(tenant); return 503 + "X-Fallback-Region: <resident>"
if cfg.residency == LOCAL && !cfg.allow_forwarding: return 409
if cfg.residency == LOCAL && cfg.allow_forwarding && lease_state != STABLE: // soft-state
  if cfg.allow_staging: attach_header("X-Staged-Write: true"); forward_to_staging()
  else attach_header("X-Forwarded-Audit: true"); forward()
```
Mike: We should also add a rollback-triggered alert path: if controller revokes lease within T seconds of acquisition and `forwarded_writes > N`, fire a Pager with high severity. Thresholds TBD.
Ada: Operator playbook (short): 1) On swap start, prewarm tenant cache and fence any streaming sessions, 2) hold writes if probes haven't confirmed L heartbeats, 3) if lease is revoked within 30s of grant: mark tenant `resident-only`, run staging aborts, notify product and affected customers, 4) if rollback rate >1% for 5m, escalate.
Priya: Compliance note: staged write payloads for EU origin must be stored in EU-only staging buckets with ephemeral TTL (default 7d) and explicit KMS scope. We'll add tests to ensure no staging copies leave region.
Ben: SDK guidance: when client sees `X-Fallback-Region` or `409`, SDK should surface a clear error and optionally auto-retry against the given region. Add `onRegionRedirect` callback.
Mike: Metrics: `handoff.staged_writes`, `handoff.rollback_count`, `handoff.lease_revocation_latency`, `handoff.staging_bytes`. SLIs: rollback rate <0.5% and p95 latency during handoff < 400ms for tenants opting into staging.
Ada: I'll draft an RFC appendix comparing preventive vs staging with cost estimates. Priya, can you own compliance bullets? Ben, can you draft the SDK change? Mike, please own the RFC.

Ada: Thanks. Quick follow-up: add an operator endpoint to force-commit staging for emergency migrations and a read-only mode to prevent new staging writes.
Priya: noted for the compliance checklist.
Ben: Noted for SDK issue.
Mike: Taking RFC. Will include sequence diagrams, ops playbook, and sample staging schema. ETA Thu.
Ada: Great, closing this sync.
